page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is an ESv5-series virtual machine configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs and 672.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

This virtual machine is heavily memory-optimized, providing an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 28.0 GB per vCPU. While the server does not include any local SSD storage, it is Premium Storage capable, allowing high-performance external disk attachments. The virtual machine runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPU hardware.

In benchmark testing, the E96-24s_v5 demonstrates strong memory performance, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25 percent and a large-block write memory bandwidth of 106.74 GB/sec, also placing in the top 25 percent. CPU-bound benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, fall within the average range. The server achieved 23.93 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and 122.74 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B LLM.

The qualitative cost profile of the E96-24s_v5 reflects its high memory density relative to compute resources, making it a cost-efficient choice for memory-bound workloads that do not require proportional CPU scaling. The absence of local storage represents a tradeoff, requiring external storage configuration. This server is highly suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
